name: Chapakura
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Chapacuran language of Bolivia; only d'Orbigny 1839 and later classification works; no phonological description

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005 [updated]. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: CHAPAKURA.
sources.note: Bibliography only; for chapakura proper cites Créqui-Montfort & Rivet 1913 and Loukotka; lists Angenot & Angenot-de Lima 1998 'A reconstrução do peso silábico e da acentuação lexical em Proto-Chapakura' (Actas III JLA: 239-249).

sources.citation: Angenot-de Lima, Geralda & Jean-Pierre Angenot. 2000. O sistema prosódico Panchapakura de demarcação lexical. In H. van der Voort & S. van de Kerke (eds.), Indigenous Languages of Lowland South America (ILLA 1), 149-164. Leiden: CNWS.
sources.note: Instrumental study of 300 cognates in five LIVING Chapakura languages (Miguelenho, Moré, Oro Win, Wari' dialects, Kuyubi); extinct Chapakura not measured. Family-level claim only.
sources.venue: Indigenous Languages of Lowland South America (ILLA 1)

sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, Georges de & Paul Rivet. 1912. Linguistique bolivienne. Le groupe Otuké. Journal de la Société des Américanistes de Paris, n.s. 9: 317-337 (p. 318 n. 2, transcription conventions used for all d'Orbigny vocabularies).
sources.note: Defines the diacritics: 'ó = eu français', 'ú = u français', and 'nous indiquons par les signes à, ẽ, ĩ, õ, des voyelles qui, d'après d'Orbigny, ont le son «nasal et guttural» du Guarani' — i.e. accents mark vowel quality/nasality, no tonic-accent notation (the scanned text).

sources.citation: Lexibank CLDF dataset birchallchapacuran (doculect 'tapakura' = chap1269, 84 forms, all from CrequiMontfortRivet1913).
sources.note: Segmented forms (waja, awimo, kowikon, mitʃitikon, witip..) carry no stress marks; data only.
Chapacura (Huachi, Tapacura) listed as extinct, Blanco River / Lake Chitiopa; no phonology or stress statement; cites Loukotka 1968, Angenot 1997, Birchall et al. 2013/2016.

sources.citation: Angenot-de Lima, Geralda. 1997. Fonotática e fonologia do lexema Protochapakura. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Federal de Rondônia, Guajará-Mirim.
sources.note: §1.3 p.12: Chapakura (Huachi, Tapakura) attested by 23 words (d'Orbigny 1839), 24 words (Cardús 1886), 436 words (Créqui-Montfort & Rivet 1913). p.13: 'As seis línguas mortas (Chapakura, Napeka, Kitemoka, Torá, Urupá e Yaru) nunca tiveram seus sistemas fonológicos descritos'. §2.2 pp.23-24 states a FAMILY-level rule: 'Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico.. o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível.. (a) uma sílaba leve é átona.. (b) uma sílaba pesada é tônica.. /#(σ)σ#/ → [(σ̀) ˈσ́]'. §3.6 'Fonemas e sons do Chapakura (Wachi)' (the text layersource:…
sources.venue: Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Federal de Rondônia, Guajará-Mirim

sources.citation: Créqui-Montfort, Georges de & Paul Rivet. 1913. Linguistique bolivienne. La famille linguistique Čapakura. Journal de la Société des Américanistes de Paris, n.s. 10: 119-171.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or pronunciation. Comparative vocabulary (Iten / Pawumwa / Čapakura Ci = d'Orbigny MS 436 words, Co = Cardús / Kitemoka / Napeka) plus lexical-concordance lists and Mure/Rokorona texts. p. 125 n. 7 refers transcription conventions to the 1912 Otuké paper. Diacritics in the wordlist (e.g. tupaká-ci, akúpa, panató) are vowel-quality marks by that convention, not stress marks. Article starts at the scanned text; PDF at Persée blocked by altcha, so the Internet Archive scanned of the whole volume was used.

sources.citation: d'Orbigny, Alcide Dessalines. 1839. Voyage dans l'Amérique méridionale, t. IV, 1re partie: L'homme américain (de l'Amérique méridionale), considéré sous ses rapports physiologiques et moraux. Paris: Pitois-Levrault.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'NATION CHAPACURA' (pp. 288-290, the scanned text) has one paragraph on the language: 'La langue est, pour la forme des mots, entièrement distincte de celles des Chiquitéens; quoiqu'assez dure, on aime pourtant à l'entendre. Elle contient beaucoup de finales terminées par des voyelles; mais aussi quelques-unes par les consonnes n, m, t, p et j' (consonants partly garbled in scanned), plus the guttural j, nasal n, body-part suffix -chi, no gender/plural marking, numerals to ten. Comparative remarks pp. 282-283 (finals, 'Les idiomes chapacura et moxo n'ont aucun son composé')…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page chap1269 (references 121928 d'Orbigny 1839; 100777 Chamberlain 1912; 144708 Montaño Aragón 1987; 554211 Birchall, Dunn & Greenhill 2016).
sources.note: No descriptive reference; all four refs typed wordlist/overview/comparative. Status 'Extinct'.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua, Michael Dunn & Simon Greenhill. 2016. A combined comparative and phylogenetic analysis of the Chapacuran language family. International Journal of American Linguistics 82(3): 255-284.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The modern comparative treatment of the family; would show how the Tapakura/Chapakura data were interpreted and whether any prosodic reconstruction is offered. Unlikely to contain a Chapakura-specific stress statement (abstract is about segments and cognates), but it supersedes 1913 as the standard reference.

tone.quote: We identify multiple systematic sound correspondences and 285 cognate sets of basic vocabulary using the available documentation. These allow us to reconstruct a large portion of the Proto-Chapacuran phonemic inventory and identify tentative major subgroupings.
tone.locator: p. 255, abstract; tone/stress terms absent throughout pp. 255-284 (section 4.1 'On the Proto-Chapacuran phonemic inventory' is segmental only)
tone.citation_as_reported: Birchall, Joshua, Michael Dunn & Simon J. Greenhill. 2016. A combined comparative and phylogenetic analysis of the Chapacuran language family. International Journal of American Linguistics 82(3): 255-284.
